question: How many three-digit numbers satisfy the property that the middle digit is the average of the first and the last digits?
solution:
Choose the first digit from 1 through 9. Its average with the last digit is an integer exactly when the two digits have the same parity. Among the digits 0 through 9, five are even and five are odd, so each first digit has five possible last digits. Each pair determines exactly one middle digit, since the average lies between the two digits. The count is 9 · 5 = 45.
Final answer: 45
